options.name: All-or-Nothing Thinking
options.default_note: You see things in black-and-white extremes: if your performance falls short of perfect, you see yourself as a total failure.

options.name: Overgeneralization
options.default_note: You draw broad conclusions from a single event, often using words like "always" or "never".

options.name: Mental Filter
options.default_note: You dwell on the negative and ignore the positive, seeing only the downside as if through tinted lenses.

options.name: Disqualifying the Positive
options.default_note: You reject positive experiences by insisting that they "don't count".

options.name: Jumping to Conclusions - Mind Reading
options.default_note: Without evidence you assume you know what others are thinking, usually that they judge you negatively.

options.name: Jumping to Conclusions - Fortune Telling
options.default_note: You predict that things will turn out badly and treat that prediction as an established fact.

options.name: Magnification and Minimization
options.default_note: You exaggerate your mistakes or others' achievements while shrinking your own strengths or others' shortcomings.

options.name: Emotional Reasoning
options.default_note: You take your feelings as proof of reality: "I feel it, so it must be true."

options.name: "Should" Statements
options.default_note: You use "I should…" or "I shouldn't…" to demand things of yourself or others, which breeds guilt or anger.

options.name: Labeling
options.default_note: You attach a fixed, negative label to yourself or others instead of describing the specific behavior.

options.name: Personalization
options.default_note: You blame yourself for negative external events even when you were not responsible for them.
